question: Which Article assigns the responsibility of calling for elections in a state to the Election Commission?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 324**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Article 324** of the Indian Constitution vests the superintendence, direction, and control of the preparation of electoral rolls and the conduct of elections to the Election Commission of India (ECI).
 
• This article empowers the Election Commission to conduct elections for Parliament, State Legislatures, and the offices of the President and Vice-President of India.
 
• The Election Commission ensures free, fair, and impartial elections in the country as mandated under this article.
 
• The Election Commission, under Article 324, is an independent constitutional authority to manage electoral processes in India.
 
• Article 324 is the cornerstone of the electoral system in India, ensuring democracy through periodic elections.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Article 326**

 
 
• Article 326 of the Indian Constitution provides for **universal adult suffrage** as the basis for elections to the Lok Sabha and State Legislative Assemblies.
 
• It states that every citizen of India who is 18 years of age or above and not disqualified under any law is eligible to vote.
 
• This article plays a key role in ensuring democratic participation by granting voting rights to all eligible citizens.
 
 
 
• **Article 327**
 
 
• Article 327 empowers the Parliament to make laws concerning all matters related to elections to Parliament and State Legislatures.
 
• It includes legislation on the preparation of electoral rolls, the delimitation of constituencies, and other election-related procedures.
 
• Laws such as the Representation of the People Act, 1950, and 1951 are enacted under the provisions of this article.
 
 
 
• **Article 325**
 
 
• Article 325 prohibits discrimination in electoral rolls on grounds of religion, race, caste, sex, or any other basis.
 
• It ensures that all citizens are treated equally concerning their inclusion in the electoral rolls.
 
• This article safeguards the principle of equality in the electoral process.
